subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser private-network confirmation/allowlist/temporary-grant SSRF policy, and what exact security semantics should govern metadata endpoints, redirects, timeouts, logging, and proxy-routed browser profiles?
rationale: The source shows the static SSRF primitive exists, but the request changes a security-sensitive browser egress boundary and public config/UX contract that automation should not define.

options.title: Approve staged SSRF policy
options.body: Define allow/block semantics, non-overridable metadata handling, timeout/rate-limit behavior, audit logging, and migration-safe config before implementing the first phase.

options.title: Approve confirmation UX now
options.body: Commit directly to an interactive approval flow and session/timeout state across browser navigation paths before implementation begins.

options.title: Keep static policy only
options.body: Leave browser SSRF as strict default plus hostname exceptions and broad trusted-environment opt-in unless maintainers explicitly reopen the direction.

recommendation.title: Approve staged SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Define allow/block semantics, non-overridable metadata handling, timeout/rate-limit behavior, audit logging, and migration-safe config before implementing the first phase.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest sampled history across browser SSRF defaults, navigation guard behavior, docs, and related security-boundary decisions.
